description:
​We are team Duality, building a web-based Space Mission Design Game for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge!
​Project Concept: An interactive web game where players act as Mission Commanders, managing resources (Budget, Fuel, Mass, Oxygen) to launch successful space missions while making decision-based choices.
​Tech Stack: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript / React.

​Looking For: Creative minds interested in frontend design, UI/UX, or game logic!
summary: ORBITAL: Mission Architect is a browser-based 2D space mission design game. Players choose a mission (Earth observation, lunar reconnaissance or Mars atmosphere study), build a spacecraft from eight subsystems, and see mass, power, cost, reliability and science value update live. An engineering check explains why a design fails, for example a power deficit, mass limit, missing communication range or unsupported instrument. Players then launch and fly the mission: deploy solar panels, point at the Sun or the target, run the instrument, transmit data and respond to simulated faults such as radiation upsets, orbit decay, comm blackouts and power spikes. A scored mission report gives a grade and lessons learned. Campaign progress is saved. The game teaches real trade-offs between mass, power, propulsion, communications and science return, and it uses NASA planetary fact sheet values to shape each destination.
details: What it does: A complete mission loop (select, design, validate, launch, operate, report, replay) with Quick Mission, Campaign and Sandbox modes. How it works: Every part has mass, power, cost, reliability and capability values. Orbit-average solar power (about 35% eclipse), battery reserve, onboard storage, propulsion tier and antenna range are simulated. Win and fail conditions depend on the player's design and commands. Benefits: Beginners learn why spacecraft engineering is about trade-offs, and failed designs explain themselves. Tools: HTML, JavaScript and Canvas 2D in a single file. No backend. Progress is saved in localStorage. Creativity: Procedurally drawn planets and spacecraft sprites (no image files), animated panel deployment and thruster flames, and fault events that need player decisions. Limits: Component stats and fault events are original game balancing, not NASA data. Time is compressed.
